Chandrayaan-3: India's Lunar Exploration Mission and Soft Landing Achievement

Launch Date: July 14, 2023 Landing Date: August 23, 2023 Launch Vehicle: LVM3-M4 Launch Site: SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota

Chandrayaan-3 is a follow-on mission to Chandrayaan-2 to demonstrate end-to-end capability in safe landing and roving on the lunar surface.

It consists of an indigenous Lander module (Vikram), Propulsion module, and a Rover (Pragyan) with an objective of developing and demonstrating new technologies required for inter-planetary missions.

Scientific Payloads

  • ChASTE (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment) to measure thermal conductivity and temperature.
  • RAMBHA (Radio Anatomy of Moon Bound Hypersensitive ionosphere and Atmosphere) to measure near-surface plasma density.
  • ILSA (Instrument for Lunar Seismic Activity) for measuring seismicity around landing site.
  • APXS & LIBS on Pragyan Rover for in-situ elemental composition determination.
